Battery maintenance cost with FULLY NESTED preprocessing and the task in cycles (convention C; post hoc, exploratory).
Plan fixed and hashed before the run: kam/PHASE3_4_PLAN.md, section 4a.

Same renewal-reward model, lead times (0, 15, 30, 45 cycles), cost ratios (5, 10, 20, 50), splits (cv1-cv5 by cell,
seed 2026; lobo1-lobo3), inner folds and bootstrap rule as audit_battery_cost2.py (convention B), with two differences:
  1. every inner training subset builds its own blocks, z-score statistics and models with kappa by the protocol rule
     computed from that subset (inner validation cells are predicted in their own blocks); the final models use kappa by
     the rule from the outer training set (as audit_battery_physical.py, 'rule_nested');
  2. the task is in cycles (the engine task scaled by three): H in {30, 45, 60, 90, 120} cycles, window [-39, +6] cycles,

     span and debounce in blocks. A model in blocks of kappa uses every cycle quantity divided by kappa.
Alarm tables are converted to cycles (remaining life at the alarm, alarm cycle and life times the kappa of the model that
produced them) and concatenated over the inner folds, so training cost rates of folds with different kappa are summed in
cycles. Capacity policies fit nothing; their settings are chosen on the training cells in blocks of the outer kappa.
Check R4a: the window-tuned recipe at H = 60 cycles reproduces the per-cell first warnings of audit_battery_physical.py
('rule_nested'); written to out/audit/cost_battery_nested_check.txt.

audit_battery_physical.py.doc:
Battery analyses with a common PHYSICAL task and fully nested preprocessing (post hoc; exploratory).

Task, in charge-discharge cycles (the protocol task at kappa = 3): warning level H = 60 cycles, acceptance window
[-39, +6] cycles on the error (estimate - true remaining life), caps {120, 180, 270} cycles, shift grid -36 ... +24 cycles
(step 1.5). Smoothing span m and debounce k are counted in blocks. A model working in blocks of kappa cycles uses
H / kappa, [-39 / kappa, +6 / kappa], caps / kappa and shifts / kappa, so every setting has the same meaning in cycles and
every score is the same physical acceptance rule (alarms can only be raised at block ends).

Fully nested: inside each outer training set, every inner training subset builds its own blocks (missing first blocks
filled from that subset), its own z-score statistics and its own regressor; the inner validation units are scored in their
own blocks. Out-of-fold in-window counts of the inner folds are summed per setting (same physical grid). After selection,
blocks, statistics and regressor are rebuilt from the complete outer training set and the outer test units are scored once.

For every outer split (cv1..cv5 by cell, seed 2026; lobo1..lobo3, one batch held out) and every kappa in KS the script
stores the inner out-of-fold predictions and the outer test predictions, then derives:
  fixed_kappa      kappa fixed in advance (2, ..., 6), inner and outer
  rule_nested      kappa = max(1, round(median life / 209.5)) computed from each inner training subset (inner folds) and
                   from the outer training set (final model): no failure life outside a training subset enters its time scale
  cv_selected      kappa chosen among KS by the summed inner out-of-fold count (ties: rule kappa of the outer training set,
                   then smaller kappa)
and, on the same task and blocks, the capacity-trend baseline (extrapolation of block-mean discharge capacity to 0.88 Ah,
same trigger; window length, span, debounce and shift chosen on the training cells).
Output: out/audit/battery_physical.csv (one row per outer split, variant, kappa and test cell)
Usage: python audit_battery_physical.py [cv|lobo|all]

audit_cost.py.doc:
Audit of the maintenance-cost comparison and of assumption A1 of Proposition 1 (post hoc; exploratory).

Same outer folds, inner folds, seeds, model, features and renewal-reward cost model as rev_experiments.py. For every
(dataset, lead time l, cost ratio rho) the following policies are tuned on the training units' out-of-fold (OOF)
predictions and applied once to the test units:
  age            optimal age replacement, age chosen on training lives
  STW_window     settings (cap, span, debounce, shift) tuned to the window for each warning level H in {10,...,40};
                 H chosen by training cost (the policy therefore also uses cost, but only to choose among 5 levels)
  STW_cost       cap, span, debounce and alarm threshold tau in {1,...,60} chosen to minimise the training cost rate
  STW_cost_1se   same grid; one-standard-error rule: among settings whose training cost rate is within one bootstrap
                 standard error of the minimum, the one with the largest mean true remaining life at the alarm
  STW_cost_q80   same grid; minimise the 80th percentile of the bootstrap distribution of the training cost rate
  Q10_cost       probabilistic alarm: gradient-boosted 10 % quantile of remaining life (pinball loss, same
                 hyperparameters, target capped at the largest cap); alarm when the smoothed quantile stays <= tau for k
                 cycles; span, k, tau chosen to minimise the training cost rate
  Q10_cost_1se   same with the one-standard-error rule
  HI_cost        health-indicator threshold alarm (as rev_experiments.py), cost-tuned
  capacity_cost, capacity_cost_1se   (battery only) threshold on the measured discharge capacity, cost-tuned
  perfect_foresight, run_to_failure  reference bounds
Bootstrap: 200 resamples of the training units (seed 2026 + fold). Battery: training-only block length kappa per fold
(audit_confirmations.py) and lead times in cycles {0, 15, 30, 45}, converted to blocks; engines: lead times {0, 5, 10, 15}.
Assumption A1: for the test units of each fold, with the window-tuned settings at H = 20, the shift is varied over the grid
and the alarm time, the unshifted error eps at the alarm and the realised in-window indicator are recorded.
Usage: python audit_cost.py DATASET [DATASET ...]      Output: out/audit/cost_<ds>.csv, out/audit/shift_<ds>.pkl

bayes_phys.py.doc:
Physics-informed Bayesian degradation model (exponential degradation path, Gebraeel-style) for the [-13, +2] window.

Health indicator (HI): linear combination of regime-normalised sensors, learned on FIT engines so that HI ~ 0 early in life
and ~ 1 at failure. Physics: HI(s) = a + exp(theta + beta * s) + noise; the engine fails when the path reaches its
failure level D. Population prior over (a, theta, beta, log D) = multivariate normal fitted to per-engine least-squares fits
of the FIT engines. For a test engine observed up to cycle t, posterior by importance sampling (likelihood of the observed HI
path, and the constraint that it has not yet failed); RUL distribution = crossing time - t. Window decoder chooses c maximising
P(c - 2 <= RUL <= c + 13). Calibration engines choose the noise scale (tempering) and a decoder shift, pooled over 30/50/70/90 %.
Same engine-level folds as the main study; test engines are scored once at t = floor(L/2).

contrib/cat.py.doc:
Certified alarm thresholds (CAT): unit-level conformal calibration of threshold-crossing end-of-life alarms.

Plan fixed and hashed before any run: contrib/PLAN.md, contrib/PLAN.sha256. Exploratory, plan hashed before the run.

A threshold-crossing alarm with smoothed estimate x_1, x_2, ... and debounce k fires at the first t at which x has stayed
<= tau for k consecutive cycles (rev_experiments.first_idx). With m_t = min_{s <= t} max(x_{s-k+1}, ..., x_s) (the
debounced running minimum), the alarm for tau fires at the first t with m_t <= tau, so the alarm time is non-increasing in
tau (Lemma 1). A replacement is planned iff the alarm leaves more than the lead time l (and, on a decision grid of step dT,
iff the next decision point is before failure); the set of admissible alarm times is {t <= t_max}. Hence

    unplanned failure at threshold tau  <=>  tau < tau*,   tau* = m_{t_max}   (critical threshold; Lemma 2)

and the order statistic tau_hat = S_(ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))) of the critical thresholds of n exchangeable calibration units
gives P(failure of a new unit) <= alpha (Theorem 1). Everything here works on the alarm tables of rev_experiments
(U, ok, ya, ta, L) so that every decision and every cost is identical to the existing cost code.

functions.name: runmin
functions.doc: Debounced running minimum m_t = min_{s<=t} max(x_{s-k+1..s}); +inf before k values exist.

functions.name: alarm_index
functions.doc: Index of the first alarm for every threshold in thr (len(x) if never); identical to rev_experiments.first_idx.

functions.name: last_admissible
functions.doc:
Largest index i at which an alarm still gives a planned replacement, -1 if none.
y: true remaining life at cycles 1..L-1 (model units; strictly decreasing); scale converts model units to cycles
(battery blocks); lead in cycles. dT None: planned iff y_i * scale > lead (rev_experiments.cost_of).
dT given: planned iff g(t_i) + lead < L with t_i = (i + 1) * scale,
g(t) = max(dT, ceil(t/dT) dT). At lead 0 this is kam_fd001.grid_cost.

functions.name: critical_threshold
functions.doc: Closed form of Lemma 2: tau* = m_{t_max} (continuous), +inf if no admissible alarm time.

functions.name: planned_matrix
functions.doc: (U, T) boolean: planned replacement for every unit and every threshold column of an alarm table (cycles).

functions.name: scores_from_table
functions.doc: Critical threshold on the grid: smallest tau in taus with a planned replacement (+inf if none). Checks Lemma 1.

contrib/cat_sim.py.doc:
Phase 1: ground-truth checks of the certified alarm threshold (CAT) on simulated data (contrib/PLAN.md, Phase 1).

Part A  Theorem 1 (validity). Calibration units and new units are drawn i.i.d. from a large simulated pool, so the
        failure probability of a calibrated threshold is known exactly under the pool distribution: P(S > tau_hat).
        A1  virtual RUL simulator of Kamariotis et al. (their Sec. 3; T_F ~ N(225, 40), correlated lognormal errors,
            decisions at t_k = 10k), point estimate = median of the predictive distribution, lead l in {0, 10}.
        A2  monotone-degradation model (below), 1-cycle decisions, lead l in {0, 5, 10, 15}, one setting.
        n in {20, 50, 100, 200}, alpha in {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10}, 20,000 replicates per cell; scores on the threshold
        grid (ties; Theorem 1 gives P <= alpha) and continuous (also P > alpha - 1/(n+1)). Criterion (plan): realised
        P in [alpha - 1/(n+1) - 3 MCSE, alpha + 3 MCSE] (lower end for continuous scores only). Descriptive: the
        per-time-step conformal lower bound (threshold l + q_{1-alpha} of the residuals x_t - r_t over all cycles).
Part B  Theorem 2 (fragility as selection), degradation model: plain minimisation of the training cost rate over G
        settings (G in {1, 4, 12, 36}, nested subsets of 36 correlated settings, or G independent noise realisations of
        one setting) and the threshold grid, rho in {50, 1000}, l in {0, 10}; realised P(fail) of the selected policy
        against min(1, G/(n+1)) and 1/(n+1); true cost rates of plain tuning and of CAT-c (alpha = 0.05, one setting).
Part C  Secondary: coverage of 95% intervals for M (simulator A1, sigma = 0.4): their Eq. 7, the paired influence
        interval and the paired bootstrap (2,000 resamples), n in {20, 100}, 5,000 replicates, truth from n = 200,000.

Monotone-degradation model (fixed before the run): life L ~ round(N(200, 40)) clipped to [100, 400]; shape
beta ~ U(1.5, 3); degradation D_t = (t / L)^beta reaches 1 at failure; observation z_t = D_t + 0.04 e_t, e_t ~ N(0, 1).
Estimate of the remaining life at t: least-squares line through the last w observations (fewer than 3 points or slope
<= 1e-4: 300), RUL_hat = clip((1 - fitted level at t) / slope, 0, 300); causal EWM span m; debounce k. Settings
w in {10, 20, 40}, m in {1, 3, 6}, k in {1, 2, 3, 5} (36, like the recipe's 3 x 3 x 4 grid); primary setting (20, 3, 2).
Seeds: A1 2026 (sigma = 0.4) and 2027 (sigma = 0.15); degradation pools 9000 (correlated settings) and 9001 (independent
realisations); replicate draws 9100 + cell index; Part C 9200. Outputs in out/contrib/: sim_validity.csv,
sim_selection.csv, sim_m_coverage.csv, sim_checks.txt.
Usage: python contrib/cat_sim.py [A|B|C ...]   (default: all)

countdown_hmm.py.doc:
Countdown HMM for remaining-useful-life (RUL) on PHM08 — still a discrete HMM.

States
  r = 0 .. Rc-1 : "r cycles left"   (deterministic countdown r -> r-1)
  H             : "healthy, >= Rc cycles left"  (leaves H with an age-dependent
                  hazard learned from the training engines' lifetimes)
Observations
  one discrete symbol per cycle (1..M): a learned health index (ridge regression
  of all regime-normalised, engine-baseline-corrected sensors onto
  min(RUL, Rc)/Rc), cut into M quantile bins.
Inference
  forward filtering -> posterior over the current state -> full RUL distribution
  (H mass spread using the training life distribution given the engine's age)
Decision
  predicted RUL = value that minimises the EXPECTED PHM08 score under that
  distribution (so it is automatically cautious);  90% interval = 5th..95th pct.

Head-to-head: our end-of-life warning model vs re-implementations of the three published PHM08 challenge approaches,
all under ONE identical first-warning protocol (window [-13, +2], error = prediction - true RUL).

  FIT engines  -> train the RUL model
  CAL engines  -> choose the warning settings: smoothing span, debounce k, shift s (+ the method's own option below)
  TEST engines -> first warning = first cycle where the smoothed, shifted prediction stays <= H for k cycles; scored once.
Methods
  ours       capped gradient-boosted trees on causal features of 15 sensors; cap in {40, 60, 90} chosen on CAL
  similarity trajectory-similarity RUL, in the spirit of Wang et al. (2008)   [median of the RUL distribution]
  rnn        LSTM network (stored predictions of the main pipeline), in the spirit of Heimes (2008)
  mlp_kf     multilayer perceptron + Kalman filter over time, in the spirit of Peel (2008); filter noise ratio chosen on CAL
  cnn        1-D CNN (stored predictions; later deep-learning baseline, Li et al. 2018 style)
These are re-implementations in the spirit of the published methods, not the original code.

hybrid_tf.py.doc:
Hybrid Transformer + engineered-feature model, and distributional GBM, for the [-13, +2] window at half of life.

Error = prediction - true RUL; correct iff -13 <= error <= +2  <=>  true RUL in [pred - 2, pred + 13].
Protocol: same engine-level 5-fold CV and fit/calibration split as the main study (seeds 2026 / 7).
  FIT engines  : train models (all cycles, uncapped RUL target)
  CAL engines  : early stopping of the network; choice of decoder shift
  TEST engines : scored once at t = floor(L/2).
Both models predict 9 quantiles of the RUL; the window decoder picks the prediction c that maximises the predicted
probability P(c - 2 <= RUL <= c + 13) (Bayes-optimal for the window). No step sees a test engine's total life.

kam/kam_metric.py.doc:
Re-implementation of the decision-oriented metric M of Kamariotis, Tatsis, Chatzi, Goebel & Straub (2024),
Reliability Engineering & System Safety 242, 109723 (arXiv:2306.03759v2), replacement-only decision setting (their
Section 2.3). Equation numbers refer to arXiv v2. This is a re-implementation from the paper; the authors' code is not
available, and nothing here reproduces their numbers.

Conventions (theirs):
  * decisions only at t_k = k * dT, k = 1, 2, ...; a preventive replacement decided at t_k happens at t_k;
  * cost c_p for a preventive replacement at T_R < T_F, c_c for a corrective replacement at the failure time T_F;
  * life-cycle length T_lc = min(T_R, T_F)                                                        (Eq. 8)
  * R_hat = mean(C_m) / mean(T_lc)                                                                 (Eq. 2)
  * perfect policy: preventive replacement at the last grid point strictly before T_F               (Sec. 2.3.1, Eq. 4)
  * M_hat = (R_hat - R_perfect) / R_perfect                                                        (Eq. 6, 9)
  * Var[R_hat] by the first-order (delta-method) formula                                           (Eq. 3)
  * Var[M_hat] = Var[R_hat] / R_perfect^2, the variance of R_perfect being neglected               (Eq. 7)
Sample moments use ddof = 1 (the paper does not state the estimator).

M >= 0 is NOT enforced: m_hat() records every negative value in VIOLATIONS (with a label) and returns it unchanged.
A negative M arises (i) for a policy that acts between grid points, and (ii) in the case of their footnote 1, when c_c is
so close to c_p that letting a unit fail beats replacing it at the last grid point; perfect_with_failure_option() checks
(ii) explicitly.

kam/kam_simulator.py.doc:
Phase 1b: check of the metric re-implementation on the virtual RUL simulator of Kamariotis et al. (2024), Section 3
(arXiv:2306.03759v2), replacement-only setting. Qualitative comparison with their Figs. 4 and 5 only.

Simulator (their Eqs. 21-25): T_F ~ N(225, 40); decision points t_k = 10k; ln RUL_pred,k ~ N(mu_k, sigma) with
mu_k = ln(T_F - t_k) + ln eps_k, (ln eps_1, ...) ~ MVN(0, Sigma), Sigma_ij = sigma^2 exp(-|t_i - t_j| / 50);
sigma = 0.4 (their Fig. 4) and 0.15 (Fig. 5); n = 2000 components; c_p = 1, c_c = c_p / ratio.
Policies (their Sec. 2.3.2-2.3.4):
  1  replace at t_k if Pr(RUL_pred,k <= dT) >= p_thres, with p_thres = c_p/c_c and with p_thres minimising M on the same
     2000 components (in-sample, as in their Sec. 3.2);
  2  replace at t_k if the minimiser T_R* of Eq. (12) satisfies T_R* <= t_k + dT;
  3  as 2 with the objective of Eq. (14), E[C]/E[T] of the population set by their option 1 (optimal age replacement for
     N(225, 40)).
T_R is optimised on a log-spaced grid of x = T_R - t_k (400 points from 0.05 to 5000 cycles plus every 0.05 cycle in
[9, 11]); the decision only depends on whether the minimiser lies at or below dT.
Output: out/kam/sim_results.csv (one row per sigma, ratio, policy), out/kam/sim_pthres.csv, out/kam/sim_checks.txt

theory_check.py.doc:
Empirical check of the window-centring proposition.

Model: a warning is raised when the shifted prediction p + s first falls to H; at that moment the unshifted prediction error is
eps = p - r (r = true remaining life), and the reported error is e = eps + s. With eps ~ F (continuous, unimodal, symmetric about
its median m) the probability of a correct first warning is P(s) = F(b - s) - F(a - s); it is maximised at s* = (a + b)/2 - m
(= -5.5 - m for the window [-13, +2]), and the maximum equals P(|eps - m| <= (b - a)/2).
For every dataset and warning level we compute, on the TEST warnings (one per engine), eps = pred - shift - y, its median m, the
implied s*, the shifts actually chosen on training data, the centred bound P(|eps - m| <= 7.5), the best fixed-shift rate
max_s P(a <= eps + s <= b) and the realised in-window rate. Missed engines count as failures in all rates.
Output: out/theory/theory_check.csv
